affected_system: heat-health surveillance, prevention, and care coordination
alternatives: protect minimum coverage before needs-based allocation of heat-health outreach and surge resources
adapt allocations using observed demand, uptake, and capacity for heat-health outreach and surge resources
pair risk-, access-, and minimum-coverage allocation with an explicit stop, review, and escalation rule
assumptions: Health records are privacy-preserving, population-defined, timely, and separated from service-request proxies.
Heat exposure, care seeking, reporting, and intervention effects remain distinct constructs.
All alternatives, capacities, costs, effects, thresholds, and failure scenarios are proposed until bound to evidence.
baseline: retain the current distribution rule for heat-health outreach and surge resources.

constraints.description: The heat-health surveillance and prevention allocate must respect declared minimum service, eligibility, capacity, and distributional safeguards.
Every released metric must retain evidence type, source lineage, geography, time, assumptions, and uncertainty.
No analytical output may bypass lawful authority, accountable human review, or an applicable appeal process.

decision_cadence: recompiled at each planning cycle and after material evidence change
decision_owner: public-health preparedness director and emergency medical services lead
decision_question: How should community health workers, call capacity, transport, and clinical surge slots be distributed?

independence_key.binding_constraint: The heat-health surveillance and prevention allocate must respect declared minimum service, eligibility, capacity, and distributional safeguards.
independence_key.evidence_gate: Evidence for heat-health outreach and surge resources passes documented checks for eligible denominators, group attributes, inventory, minimum-service rules, and allocation records.
independence_key.primary_outcome: high-risk people without assigned support capacity

intended_claim: A versioned allocate design for comparing declared alternatives affecting heat-health outreach and surge resources, conditional on its evidence gate.
limitations: This library record has no city binding and therefore reports no local input, output, or recommendation.
Readiness describes explicit source and method gates; it does not certify implementation feasibility.
External domain, legal, community, security, and operational review remains outside this design artifact.

objectives.metric: high-risk people without assigned support capacity
distributional gap in high-risk people without assigned support capacity
decision claims with complete evidence lineage

prohibited_claims: Do not report assigned support as contacted patients, completed visits, or improved health.
Do not describe a design-only record as a city execution, deployment, adopted policy, or impact result.
Do not relabel proposed, estimated, simulated, optimized, or causal evidence as observed evidence.
Do not infer individual behavior, protected status, harm, or entitlement from aggregate records.

release_gate.failure_release: Release an explicit insufficient-evidence record naming missing sources, failed diagnostics, prohibited claims, and the next validation action.
release_gate.pass_condition: Evidence for heat-health outreach and surge resources passes documented checks for eligible denominators, group attributes, inventory, minimum-service rules, and allocation records.

title: Allocate heat-health outreach and clinical surge support
transportability_risks: Clinical coding, surveillance coverage, acclimatization, housing, and care access vary.
Small-area health estimates may be unstable or disclosure-sensitive.
